clue.text: A big book hotel's kept in reception

indicators.note: something kept in another is held inside it, so the hotel letter goes inside the book

blocks.note: taken as written
a tome is a large, weighty book
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hefty volume sits on the desk in a hotel's reception area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reception' looks like part of the hotel picture, but it is the definition: an at-home is a party where guests are received.
explanation.definitionFit: An at-home is an informal social gathering held at the host's house, a kind of reception for visitors.

clue.text: Murder victim in noisy situation, first off

indicators.note: with the first taken off, the opening letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a babel is a confused din of voices, after the Tower of Babel

explanation.surface: A detective story where someone is killed amid a racket, the first clue gone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abel is killed by his brother Cain, the first murder victim in the Bible.

clue.text: Old soldier's aspiration, inflamed within

indicators.note: within says one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: an aspiration is a hope
inflamed in the sense of set alight

explanation.surface: A veteran's ambition has been fired up from inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition carries the 's: the clue reads 'Old soldier is ...', with the wordplay following.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoplite was a heavily armed infantryman of ancient Greece, so an old soldier indeed.

clue.text: Masculinity of Scot, having his moment

blocks.note: Mac is a common nickname for a Scotsman
taken as written
mo is short for moment, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: A Scotsman enjoys his moment of showing off how manly he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is aggressive or exaggerated pride in being a man, a show of masculinity.

clue.text: Plant is better with strange music

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual order

blocks.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener claims plants grow better when strange music is played to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the definition to the wordplay; it is not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsicum is the pepper plant genus, grown for sweet and chilli peppers.

clue.text: Choir ceased working in province

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked over into a new form

blocks.note: all eleven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A choir has stopped singing somewhere in the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like the opposite of 'ceased', which is the joke of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdiocese is the district under an archbishop, the church's term for an ecclesiastical province.

clue.text: Second religious summary, a lengthy read

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a creed is a summary statement of religious belief

explanation.surface: A second summary of the faith turns out to be a long slog to get through.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, often tedious piece of writing, the sort that takes ages to read.

clue.text: Instrument hit accidentally in research establishment

indicators.note: something done accidentally comes out in no planned order
in places the jumbled word inside the name of the institution

blocks.note: CERN is the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of lab equipment gets knocked by mistake at a research centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A cithern, or cittern, is a wire-strung Renaissance instrument like a flat-backed lute.

clue.text: Wrongly says country will be involved in failure

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: a miss is a failure to hit
a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A nation will be dragged into a failure, a politician wrongly claims.
explanation.definitionFit: To misstate is to report something inaccurately, so it means wrongly says.

clue.text: Anticipate old lover wanting to get kissed audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
pecked means kissed lightly

explanation.surface: A former partner hopes for a kiss, anticipating one out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: PECKED, spoken, sounds like the last syllable of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect is to look forward to something as likely, the same as to anticipate it.

clue.text: Gathers together in a cold island needing sun

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Crete is the large Greek island
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers cluster on a chilly island, longing for sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by gradual accumulation, gathering material together layer by layer.

clue.text: Be a squatter with determination?

blocks.note: surface reading: occupy a building stubbornly, refusing to budge
setter's reading: a squatter is someone sitting down, and determination is the act of deciding a case, so sit there and rule on others

explanation.walkthrough: A sit-in is a protest occupation, which feeds the squatting picture; 'determination' means a verdict, not resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit in judgement is to act as judge over others, deciding their case while seated on the bench.

clue.text: 'Fair Earth' will come with intervention of leading protest group

indicators.note: an intervention steps in between, so one word is put into the middle of another

blocks.note: fair and just both mean even-handed
earth in the sense of ground or soil
top as in foremost or leading

explanation.surface: A slogan about a just planet is promoted by a prominent campaigning group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' looks like it describes the protest group, but it is the piece that intervenes inside the word for earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Just Stop Oil is a British climate campaign group known for disruptive direct-action protests against new fossil fuel licences.

clue.text: The fighting force first needing soldiers to get electronic device

blocks.note: taken as written
RM is the Royal Marines
1st, with the numeral read as the letter I
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An army unit must first call on troops before it can get hold of some gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermistor is a resistor whose resistance changes with temperature, a component used in electronic circuits.

clue.text: Dissenter suffering from fatigue

indicators.note: suffering suggests being knocked out of shape, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: all nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel is worn down and exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness and fatigue are both the state of lacking energy after exertion.

clue.text: Contemptible person lots backed

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: tons, as in 'tons of time', means lots

explanation.surface: A despicable figure has many supporters behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots backed' looks like a gambling picture, but lots is a synonym to be found first.
explanation.definitionFit: Snot is a slang insult for a nasty, contemptible person, from snotty meaning arrogant.

clue.text: Cat in agony given drug, a chemical compound

indicators.note: in tells us one thing sits inside another

blocks.note: agony is extreme pain
a tom is a male cat
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A cat in pain is given medication by the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a standard crossword drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are nitrogen compounds formed when protein decays, once blamed for food poisoning.

clue.text: Like old parliament game joined by politician

definitions.note: describes the Rump Parliament, the word used as a modifier

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A historical parliament is pictured as a game that a politician joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rump Parliament was what remained of the English Long Parliament after Pride's Purge of 1648.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rump was the remnant of the seventeenth-century English Parliament, so rump describes that old assembly.

clue.text: The writer on ship in a port

blocks.note: the writer is the setter, referring to themself as me
SS is steamship
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The author is aboard a ship docked at some harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a port' reads as one phrase, but 'in a' is wordplay and 'port' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is a Sicilian seaport city on the strait separating Sicily from mainland Italy.

clue.text: When nicest old girl gets nasty disease

blocks.note: as in the sense of when, 'as I left'
nicest means the best
O is the abbreviation for old
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: The sweetest old girl comes down with a horrible illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestosis is a serious lung disease caused by inhaling asbestos fibres, so a nasty disease indeed.

clue.text: Fish? Sarah's caught any number by river

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so the name wraps round the rest

blocks.note: Sal is a pet form of the name Sarah
N stands for an unspecified number in maths
the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England

explanation.surface: Sarah has landed a whole pile of catches on the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that a sand eel is a fish named like an eel, not strictly one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand eels are small slender fish that burrow in sand and are a staple food of puffins and other seabirds.

clue.text: Eastern muck – I kept being sick

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so the I sits within the word for muck

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern
muck and mess both mean dirt or disorder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes eating dodgy Eastern food and throwing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Emesis is the medical term for vomiting, the act of being sick.

clue.text: Be upset with semi-meltdown – it means someone's gutted

definitions.note: a noun phrase in effect: the act by which someone is gutted

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Someone told to be upset over a partial meltdown is left feeling gutted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' is British slang for bitterly disappointed, which suits the meltdown picture; here it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Disembowelment is removing the entrails, literally gutting a person.

clue.text: Prison housing one murderer

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, as a building holds its occupants

blocks.note: the can is slang for prison
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A jail holds a single killer.
explanation.walkthrough: This partners 1 Down: in Genesis, Cain killed his brother Abel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cain, son of Adam and Eve, is the Bible's first murderer.

clue.text: English campaign – there's an issue

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a mission is an organised campaign

explanation.surface: An English crusade turns out to have a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a problem, but it is meant as something issued or given off.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is something discharged or sent out, which is one sense of issue as a noun.

clue.text: Had to rush around tree plantations

indicators.note: turning around means facing the other way, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: had as in had dinner
to nip is to dash quickly, as in nip to the shops

explanation.surface: Someone was forced to dash round the forestry estates.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineta is the plural of pinetum, a plantation or collection of pine and other conifer trees.

clue.text: Poles, see, at infrequent intervals

blocks.note: spars are stout poles, as for masts
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Look, the posts are set only here and there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a command to look, but it is the noun for a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparsely means thinly scattered, with long gaps between, so at infrequent intervals.

clue.text: City's philosopher and songwriter

blocks.note: first meaning: the German capital
second meaning: a surname shared by philosopher Isaiah and songwriter Irving

explanation.walkthrough: Isaiah Berlin wrote on liberty; Irving Berlin wrote White Christmas. The one surname covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is Germany's capital city, and also the family name of the thinker Isaiah and the composer Irving.
